result:
Verified the three upstream sites and the Rust call graph. **The proposed rule is correct, and it is a replacement rather than an addition.**

## No function-body route requires the old fallback

Upstream's empty function body has exactly three comment-bearing seams, and none of them is the empty-list bracket lane:

- `emitBlockFunctionBodyWorker` (_tsc.js:119040-119058) calls `emitList` with **only** `768 /* SingleLineFunctionBodyStatements */` or `1 /* MultiLineFunctionBodyStatements */`. `emitNodeList`'s empty branch emits `emitTrailingCommentsOfPosition(children.pos)` / `emitLeadingCommentsOfPosition(children.end)` **only** under `format & 15360 /* BracketsMask */` (120041-120065); neither 768 nor 1 carries a bracket bit. So there is no bracket comment lane for any function body, ranged or not.
- The close brace is `writeToken(...)` (119030), not `emitTokenWithComment` — map only, no comment lane.
- That leaves `emitBodyWithDetachedComments`'s head and tail, each independently gated on `pos < 0` / `end < 0` — which your r388 endpoint work already implements outside the callback.

So `emit_empty_block_comments` has no upstream counterpart for a function body in either of its arms: arm (a) is the bracket lane that never runs for these formats, and arm (b) (rescan the original Block's `{`…`}`) has no upstream analogue at all. `if function_body { false }` is the faithful rule.

**Static blocks need no separate classification.** `emitClassStaticBlockDeclaration` (117915-117920) is `writeKeyword("static")` + `emitBlockFunctionBody(node.body)`, so a static block body *is* a function body upstream, and `is_function_body_block` already lists `ClassStaticBlockDeclaration`. The single guard covers it.

**Blast radius is fully local**: `emit_empty_block_comments` has exactly one caller, `printer.rs:8366`, inside the Block arm. Every non-function block route is untouched by construction.

Two further points in the proposal's favour:

- It **deletes** the r388 endpoint-keyed bypass condition instead of widening it — one fewer predicate to keep in sync with the head/tail conditions, and it removes the asymmetry where a synthesized-range function body took a different comment route from a ranged one.
- It closes a latent flag hole. `emit_empty_block_comments` checks only `comments_disabled()` (18234), **not** the Block's `NO_COMMENTS`. Constructors are function bodies, and upstream's `createDefaultConstructorBody` relies on `NoComments` to stop artificial class-member ranges from re-discovering class-body comments (the same hazard `emit_comments_before_close_brace` guards at 18353-18356). Arm (b) could resurrect exactly those; the guard removes the path.

## Expected diffs to watch in the 72 + 788 rerun

These are shapes where arm (a) currently emits and neither head nor tail will:

1. `function f() { /* c */ }` — same-line, not detached (`nodeLine == lastCommentLine`). Upstream drops it; you measured this in round 185. Diff expected, in the correct direction.
2. `function f() {\n    // c\n}` — **the one I would add as a control before landing.** No blank line, so the head is not detached (`nodeLine >= lastCommentLine + 2` fails) and the tail sits at the `}` token start where `getLeadingCommentRanges` collects nothing ⇒ upstream drops it. This is derived, not measured, and it is the most common real shape, so it is where a wrong reading would cost most.
3. `function f() {\n    // c\n\n}` — blank line before `}` makes the head genuinely detached, so it must still be emitted. Positive control that removing the `!statements.is_empty()` gate on the head really covers empty bodies.
4. Empty class static block with a comment — confirms the 117915 route.
5. Synthetic/default constructor body with `NoComments` over a class-member range — previously reachable through arm (b); must now emit nothing.
6. Empty System execute body with a real copied range — head at array pos, tail at EOF, and the arm-(a) overlap I flagged in round 184 disappears.

One mechanical note: with `emitted_comments` forced to `false`, empty function bodies always take the `if !emitted_comments && multi_line { write_line(false) } else { write_space(" ") }` fallthrough. That is exactly upstream's empty-list branch (`MultiLine ⇒ writeLine`, `SpaceBetweenBraces ⇒ writeSpace`), so spacing is unchanged — worth stating in the commit body since the `false` short-circuit touches spacing as well as comments.

## On the other two

The `CommentSourceRange` reuse with endpoint-keyed head / relocation / tail conditions is what I recommended and matches 121078-121080; nothing further from me until it is native-qualified.

Your r387 finding resolves the ASI case the way the route predicted: explicit `alwaysStrict:false` ⇒ offset 0 ⇒ real array range ⇒ the body tail emits one own-line comment, and `alwaysStrict:true`/`removeComments` suppress it. Tightening the unit to "count 1, on its own line, after the `exports_1` call" rather than global absence is the right repair — it keeps the invariant the test was named for (the statement must not reown it) and stops conflating the two owners. Keeping omitted-`alwaysStrict` on the upstream `true` default preserves the boundary; a probe row for the omitted case would make that explicit rather than inherited.

Scope: read-only, nothing executed. The claims above rest on `_tsc.js:119021-119058`, `117915-117920`, `120029-120065`, `121075-121101` and `printer.rs:8366`, `18330-18290`-range as committed at 70696be10; the r391 probe and your round-185 measurement are taken as reported, and I make no qualification claim for the pending 244/788 reruns.
